items.headline: Meta, Sierra and major retailers publish the Personal Agent Protocol
items.summary: Meta and Sierra, backed by Walmart, Shopify, Stripe, Genesys, Instinct and Rocket, released an open standard governing how personal AI shopping/service agents authenticate and interact with businesses. It aims to give consumers one consistent, OAuth-based way to grant agents read or write access across companies, competing with Visa's rival Trusted Agent Protocol.

items.headline: Meta deploys AI tools to catch ads that funnel users toward CSAM
items.summary: Following a Tech Transparency Project investigation, Meta rolled out an LLM-based detector aimed at ads that look benign but covertly link to child sexual abuse material elsewhere online, and said it had actioned 33.2 million pieces of child exploitation content across Facebook and Instagram in H1 2026.

items.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Argon draws internal skepticism over real-world coding
items.summary: Bloomberg reports that despite strong benchmark scores, Google employees found newly launched Gemini 4 Argon underwhelming on practical coding tasks, fueling debate over whether Google has closed the gap with Anthropic and OpenAI's latest frontier models. Initial access is limited to testers in Google's Fairwind program and cyber-defense partners.

items.headline: Nvidia in talks to deepen its stake in open-weights startup Reflection AI
items.summary: The Financial Times reported Nvidia is discussing acquiring or further investing in Reflection AI, a U.S. open-weights model developer; a deal could reportedly take the shape of an acquihire structured to sidestep antitrust scrutiny, underscoring Nvidia's push to secure footholds across the open-model ecosystem.

items.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI's revenue run-rates diverge once accounting methods are compared
items.summary: Bloomberg-sourced reporting highlights that Anthropic books gross sales through cloud-partner revenue-share deals (e.g., with Amazon and Google) while OpenAI reports only its net share, creating a roughly $25 billion gap between the two companies' headline annualized revenue figures that isn't a like-for-like comparison.

items.headline: DeepSeek reportedly raising ~¥80B as Mistral's trillion-parameter flagship enters preview
items.summary: An industry briefing says DeepSeek is in talks for a funding round of at least 80 billion yuan, while Mistral AI has put its new trillion-parameter flagship model into public preview, two signs of accelerating competition among non-US frontier model developers.

items.headline: Synopsys reportedly exploring AI partnerships with Chinese labs
items.summary: Nikkei Asia reported that chip-design software maker Synopsys is in discussions about partnering with Chinese AI labs, a move that would test the boundaries of US export controls on advanced semiconductor design tools amid tightening US-China tech tensions.

items.headline: Four robotics and physical-AI advances set to matter through 2026
items.summary: Fast Company highlights FieldAI's robot-intelligence platform for construction and manufacturing, GelSight's tactile sensors, Hexagon's stair-climbing humanoids being piloted at BMW factories, and Vigilant Aerospace's drone situational-awareness systems as the robotics developments most likely to reach real deployments this year.

items.headline: Former DeepMind researcher argues LLMs still lack genuine reasoning
items.summary: A widely discussed MIT Technology Review essay by a former Google DeepMind researcher contends that today's large language models don't truly reason, and that AlphaGo-style search architectures are needed to build auditable, verifiable reasoning rather than relying on next-token prediction alone.

items.headline: Humanoid robot reportedly reaches 60% autonomy on factory floor
items.summary: A robotics industry roundup reports a humanoid robot now performing factory assembly work with a claimed 60% autonomy rate, alongside a separate unveiling of a US-built humanlike five-fingered robotic hand ahead of an upcoming humanoid product launch.

items.headline: Walmart's warehouse automation push with Symbotic hits technical setbacks
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Walmart's large-scale automation rollout with robotics partner Symbotic has run into technical problems, a reminder that even well-funded enterprise robotics deployments face significant real-world integration challenges.

items.headline: Anthropic's SpaceX compute deal scales up to Colossus 2
items.summary: Anthropic is paying SpaceX roughly $1.25 billion a month for AI compute capacity under a multi-year deal first tied to the Colossus 1 data center in Memphis, with Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown announcing an expansion onto GB200 capacity at the newer Colossus 2 site.
